out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Designated Use
violations.observation: Observed the handsink located at the bar being used to store an empty jug container and multiple other little utensils.
violations.corrective_action: Handsinks are to be used only for washing hands to encourage proper hand washing and to prevent contamination of cleaned hands. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT EVEN IF THE HAND SINK IS NOT USED AS FREQUENTLY AS THE OTHERS, HAND SINKS MUST ALWAYS BE AVAILABLE FOR EMPLOYEES TO WASH THEIR HANDS. PIC HAD REMOVED ITEMS FROM THE SINK AT TIME OF INSPECTION.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: in the 3DR Prep Top unit, raw shell eggs were being stored above ready to eat noodles, beansprouts and chopped onion. In the Walk-in Refrigerator, raw fish was being stored above ready to eat cooked vegetables on the speed rack once first entering the walk-in refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THE PROPER WAY TO STORE RAW FOODS AND READY TO EAT FOODS. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE REMOVE THE EGGS FROM THE 3DR PREP TOP UNIT AND PLACE THEM INTO THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR. THEN PIC HAD EMPLOYEE MOVE THE RAW FISH IN THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR TO BELOW THE COOKED VEGETABLES ON THE SPEED RACK.

violations.title: Chemical Sanitization, Chlorine Requirements
violations.observation: When tested, the chlorine-based sanitizing solution was observed to be at a concentration less than what is required for effective sanitization of food-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils. Observed the sanitizing solution in the dish machine with a concentration of 0 ppm total chlorine at time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: A chlorine-based sanitizing solution shall have a minimum concentration of at least 50 to 200 ppm total chlorine when tested using the appropriate test kit. PIC WAS ABLE TO HAVE A TECHNICIAN COME IN AT TIME OF INSPECTION TO FIX DISH MACHINE SANITIZER CONCENTRATION. THE DISH MACHINE WAS WORKING PROPERLY BY END OF INSPECTION AND HAD A PPM READING OF 100PPM BEFORE END OF INSPECTION. 9PADTHAI (Inspection Date: 06/24/2026) Page 2 of 4

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: broccoli after being cooked was sitting out at room temperature on a prep top table in the kitchen. The cooked broccoli was temping at 73F at time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL FOODS THAT ARE INTENDED TO BE HOT HELD, MUST BE AT A MINIMUM TEMP OF 135F TO BE SAFE TO EAT. PIC DISCUSSED WITH EMPLOYEES ABOUT PROPER HOT HOLDING TEMPS AND THREW AWAY BROCCOLI THAT WASNOT HOT HOLDING AT THE CORRECT TEMPERATURE.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: On a prep table in an ice bath, bean sprouts were temping at 71F at time of inspection. Also, in the 3DR Prep Top unit minced garlic in oil (61F), cut cabbage (50F & 51F), fried tofu (50F), beansprouts (60F) were all not temping at time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL COLD FOODS MUST BE TEMPING AT A MAXIMUM TEMPERATURE OF 41F. DUE TO THE 3DR PREP TOP UNIT NOT WORKING PROPERLY, PIC HAD EMPLOYEE MOVE ALL FOOD FROM THE 3DR PREP TOP TO THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR AND 1DR UPR FREEZER TO RAPID COOL IN ORDER TO KEEP FOODS. PIC ALSO MOVED THE BEANSPROUTS THAT WERE COLD HOLDING ON THE PREP TABLE TO THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR TO COOL.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Poison/Toxic Material, Conditions of Use
violations.observation: Pesticides labeled for residential use were observed in the facility and are being applied by the operator to control pests. RAID was found in the kitchen at time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Remove residential use pesticides from the facility. When necessary for pest control, chemical pesticides must be applied by a certified pesticide applicator to prevent injury and contamination. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT RAID CANNOT BE USED IN COMMERCIAL KITCHENS AND ONLY APPROVED CHEMICALS CAN BE SPRAYED BY A CERTIFIED PEST CONTROL OPERATOR. PIC THREW AWAY THE CAN OF RAID AT TIME OF INSPECTION.

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers
violations.observation: Working containers of poisonous and toxic materials are not properly labeled with a common name. Spray bottles in the chemical storage area did not have proper labels on them.
violations.corrective_action: Label all working containers of poisonous and toxic materials, including cleaners and sanitizers, with a common name to prevent the dangerous misuse of these materials. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL CHEMICAL SPRAY BOTTLES MUST HAVE LABELS ON THEM ONCE TAKEN OUT OF THIER ORIGINAL CONTAINER.

violations.title: Thermometers, Location for Units with TCS foods
violations.observation: There was no temperature measuring device located in the following cold or hot holding equipment: in the 3DR PREP TOP and the 2DR PREP TOP there were no thermometers present at time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Cold or hot holding equipment used for the storage of time/temperature control for safety food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one integral or permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display. EHS DISCUSSED THAT ALL COLD HOLDING UNITS NEED A THERMOMETER PLACED INSIDE OF THEM BY TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: multiple items in squeeze bottles around the kitchen did not have labels on them at time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL FOODS TAKEN OUT OF THEIR ORIGINAL CONTAINER AND PLACED INTO A NEW ONE, MUST HAVE A LABEL ON THEM. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE BEGIN LABELING ITEMS AROUND THE KITCHEN BEFORE THE END OF THE INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage No Contamination
violations.observation: Food stored in a location where it is subject to splash, dust or other contamination as follows: Cabbage heads that was in the process of being prepped at time of inspection and the container in which the cut cabbage was being placed into was stored on top of a trash can.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination. EHS DISCUSSED WITH WORKER WHO WAS PREPPING THE CABBAGE THAT IT CANNOT BE STORED IN A CONTAINER OVER THE TRASH CAN WHILE BEING PREPPED. EMPLOYEE MOVED THE CABBAGE TO A CART NEAR BY UNTIL THEY ARE FINISHED PEPPING IT.

violations.title: Linens & Napkins, Proper Use
violations.observation: Linens (i.e. napkins, aprons, towels, table cloths) found used in direct contact with the following food item(s): a rice net was found at the time of inspection in a rice cooker while rice was being cooked. Also wet towels were being left of top of cooked noodles on a cart in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Linens may not be used in contact with food unless they are used to line a container for the service of foods and the linens are replaced each time the container is refilled for a new consumer. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT RICE NETS AND WET TOWELS ON NOODLES CAN NEVER BE USED IN FOOD PREP. PIC REMOVED THE WET TOWELS FROM THE NOODLES AND WILL STOP USING THE RICE NET MOVING FORWARD. 9PADTHAI (Inspection Date: 06/24/2026) Page 3 of 4

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: Spoons and knives were being stored in water on the stove top in a small metal container. The water the utensils were being stored in were temping at 88F and 116F at time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL UTENSILS BEING STORED IN WATER MUST BE KEPT IN WATER AT A TEMPERATURE OF 135F OR ABOVE. PIC HAD EMPLOYEE MOVE THE UTENSILS TO THE 3VAT SINK TO BE WASHED RINSED AND SANITIZED.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Multiple garlic containers, 5 gallon buckets and fish containers were being used around the kitchen to store other items inside of them.
violations.corrective_action: Single-service items may not be reused. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL SINGLE USE CONTAINERS CANNOT BE RESUED FOR OTHER FOOD ITEMS ONCE THE ORIGINAL ITEM IS GONE. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT BEOFRE NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION, ALL SINGLE USE CONTAINERS MUST BE GONE AND NEW FOOD SAFE CONTAINERS MUST BE OBTAINED.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: The 3DR PREP TOP unit was temping above 41F at time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT THE 3DR PREP TOP UNIT SHOULD BE HOLDING A TEMP OF 41F OR BELOW. EHS WILL CONDUCT A FOLLOW-UP INSPECTION TO MAKE SURE UNIT IS FIXED.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and/or smooth: Cardboard was being used to line multiple shelving units in kitchen. Cardboard was also used to line shelves inside of the 2DR prep top unit.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT CARDBOARD CAN NEVER BE USED TO LINE SHELVES IN THE KITCHEN BECAUSE IT IS NOT EASILY CLEANABLE. PIC REMOVED THE CARDBOARD FROM THE 2DR PREP TOP UNIT. PIC WILL CONTINUE TO REMOVE CARDBOARD AROUND THE KITCHEN BEFORE TIME OF NEXT ROUTINE INSPECTION.

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: Beansprouts (52).
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THE CORRECT TEMPERATURE RANGE THAT COLD FOODS SHOULD BE TEMPING AT. PIC MOVED THE BEANSPROUTS TO THE WALK-IN REFRIGERATOR TO COOL BACK TO 41F OR BELOW.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: multiple food items such as sauces and seasonings taken out of their original containers did not have labels on them.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT ALL FOODS NOT EASILY IDENTIFIABLE NEED TO HAVE PROPERLY LABELING ON THEM BY TIME OF NEXT INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items No Reuse
violations.observation: Single-service garlic containers were observed being reused for the storage of multiple food items around the kitchen in facility.
violations.corrective_action: Single-service items may not be reused. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT SINGLE USE CONTAINERS MUST NOT BE REUSED TO STORE FOODS. PIC WILL BEGIN SWITCHING OUT ALL SINGLE USE CONTAINERS BY TIME OF NEXT INSPECTION.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and/or smooth: cardboard is being used to line shelves in the walk-in refrigerator and both prep top units. Cardboard is also being used to line carts that hold food items and food preparation items.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. EHS DISCUSSED WITH PIC THAT CARDBOARD IS NOT ALLOWED TO BE USED TO LINE SHELVES BECAUSE THEY ARE NOT A MATERIAL THAT CAN BE WASHED RINSE AND SANITIZED. PIC WILL REMOVE ALL CARDBOARD BY TIME OF NEXT INSPECTION.

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Durable Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not resistant to corrosion: standard paint brushes are being used to paint on sauces and marinated for different food items.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. EHS TOLD PIC THAT STANDARD PAINT BRUSHES ARE NOT FOOD SAFE AND MUST STOP USING THEM. EHS GAVE PIC OTHER UTENSILS THAT MAY BE USED IN PLACE OF THE STANDARD PAINT BRUSHES.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Linens & Napkins, Proper Use
violations.observation: Linens (i.e. napkins, aprons, towels, table cloths) found used in direct contact with the following food item(s): cooked noodles and other mise en place for entrées on the menu.
violations.corrective_action: Linens may not be used in contact with food unless they are used to line a container for the service of foods and the linens are replaced each time the container is refilled for a new consumer. PIC NOW UNDERSTANDS THAT TOWELS CANNOT BE USED TO COVER FOOD. EHS TALKED WITH PIC ABOUT OTHER TYPES OF COVERS THAT WONT CONTAMINATE THE FOOD SUCH AS PLASTIC WRAP AND ALUMINUM FOIL. PIC TOLD EHS THEY WILL NO LONGER USE TOWELS TO COVER FOOD ITEMS MOVING FORWARD.

violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material.
